quotes.how: parsed with the same routine as scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs#intentCriteria, so every criterionText below is the intent's own text and not a paraphrase

claims.criterionText: Widened onto the fixture's recorded work, the page agent carries the five paired profiler events (`TemplateUpdate` 2/3, `LifecycleHook` 4/5, `ChangeDetection` 12/13, `Component` 18/19, `HostBindingsUpdate` 24/25), and a recorded frame with that work produces a finding listing the components in the order the profiler recorded their start events, each with the duration the page measured between its start and its matching end — and naming no component the recording does not carry.
claims.reason: The criterion is scoped to the fixture by its own opening clause - "Widened onto the fixture's recorded work" - and its facts are a frame that repeats work on demand, which no insurance-portal route produces. The repository`s verification target is the pinned zoneful portal worktree (recorded commit 976752389c22bb563d2278c2d78f423cb2505669, Angular 20.3.35), and it produces no profiler frame: extension/agent-main.js refuses a page older than 22.1.3 and refuses a zoneful page before it ever calls setProfiler, so the artefact that target lacks is a zoneless profiler stream. research/raw/m040-work-events.json records that attempt as a negative counted as a negative rather than as a capture. This task also measured the portal`s own zoneless checkout (branch claude/ai-devtools-spike, commit 92d46ec, @angular/core 22.2.2 installed and no zone.js dependency, served by `control-angular-dev-app up --target portal --dir <path>` on http://localhost:4507/) at route /home: ng.ɵsetProfiler and ng.ɵgetSignalGraph are both present, window.Zone is absent and the root injector has no NgZone provider (NG0201: No provider found for `NgZone`), so extension/agent-main.js would install on that page rather than refuse it, and one tap over a router navigation and a click recorded all five pairs with both ends (TemplateUpdate 60/60, LifecycleHook 64/64, ChangeDetection 3/3, Component 32/32, HostBindingsUpdate 26/26). That measurement is recorded in research/raw/m040-work-events.json as witness.portalZonelessAttempt with result "supported", next to the pinned zoneless refusal. So the charter`s portal clause does reach this milestone`s facts on the portal`s zoneless main, and a portal-backed verdict becomes possible the moment AGENTS.md re-pins verification to that checkout; until then a verdict taken on the pinned zoneful target would restate a refusal rather than produce a frame, and the milestone`s evidence is the recording it narrates rather than a portal frame. The evidence it rests on is research/raw/m040-work-events.json: the five pairs derived from both installed @angular/core chunks (26 values, identical in the panel's and the fixture's install), the emission sites that say what each end carries, and the witness frames the counter fixture recorded, where ComponentStart passes no identity at all and ComponentEnd passes componentView[CONTEXT]. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-narrator.test.mjs" with node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-measure.test.mjs": the first builds the finding for the recorded frame and holds the order to the start events the recording carries, and the second re-derives the pairs and the identity each end passes from the installed builds rather than from a literal. Because the portal clause reaches a feature only where a portal route can produce its facts, and no portal route on the verification target produces a profiler frame, this criterion is not-required and the recording carries it.

claims.criterionText: Recording stays additive: the four events the page agent already records keep the meaning they have today — `OutputStart` still sets the cycle trigger and `TemplateUpdateStart` still opens the cycle — and every added event travels the same per-event record shape as those four, so no surface branches on a specific event number to read one.
claims.reason: This criterion is about the page agent's own record shape: the four events it already records keep their meaning, OutputStart still sets the cycle trigger, TemplateUpdateStart still opens the cycle, and every added event travels the same per-event record. Its facts are the extension's source and the records it produces on the zoneless counter fixture, not a rendering of a portal page - and the insurance portal is not a page the agent can record on at all: the pinned target is zoneful and extension/agent-main.js refuses a zoneful page before it subscribes, so the artefact the portal lacks is the zoneless profiler stream those records come from. CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore has nothing to reach here, and the claim is carried by extension/agent-main.js and extension/performance-narrator.js. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "extension/agent-main.test.mjs" with node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-narrator.test.mjs": the first holds the agent's literal and its onEvent behaviour to the four existing meanings, and the second asserts that a worked frame reaches the narrator through one record shape and that no surface branches on an event number.

claims.criterionText: When a work interval is bracketed by a `ComponentStart`/`ComponentEnd` pair but the profiler passes no component identity for it, the finding reports cannot-tell with a named absence — that the profiler bracketed work but named no component — and never names the component by its node index, its position in the list, or its nearest named neighbour.
claims.reason: A cannot-tell with a named absence is a claim about what the profiler passed, and this milestone measured which pair forces it: research/raw/m040-work-events.json records, per pair, what each end carries at every emission site of both installed builds and what the page actually passed. ChangeDetection is the pair that carries no identity at either end - `profiler(ProfilerEvent.ChangeDetectionStart)` and `profiler(ProfilerEvent.ChangeDetectionEnd)` take no instance at all - so it is the named absence the join reports, and Component is the pair whose start passes no argument while its end passes componentView[CONTEXT], which is why the recording rules Component end-only and the narrator names its intervals from the end. The insurance portal was measured for exactly this: the pinned zoneful target refuses the agent before it subscribes (the artefact it lacks is a zoneless profiler stream), and the portal`s zoneless checkout at 92d46ec was then measured and recorded, where ComponentStart arrived with no instance on all 32 starts and ChangeDetection with none at either end - the same shape the fixture measured. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-narrator.test.mjs": its ComponentStart/ComponentEnd cases assert the named absence that stands where a component identity is missing, assert that no name is minted from a node index, a list position or a nearest named neighbour, and the frame the recording carries yields cannot-tell for exactly the intervals the recording rules as carrying no identity; node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-measure.test.mjs" re-derives the identity each end passes, from the installed builds rather than from a literal.

claims.criterionText: Every reported cost is a duration the page measured: the difference between a start event and its matching end event as recorded. A start with no matching end in the frame is reported as unmeasured, never given a duration from the next event, a reconstructed timestamp, or a clock the panel read.
claims.reason: The duration this criterion requires is the difference between a recorded start and its matching end, so its facts are a recorded frame rather than a portal page - and no duration has been measured on a portal frame: the portal`s pinned verification target produces no frame at all (extension/agent-main.js refuses a zoneful page before it calls setProfiler, so that target lacks the zoneless profiler stream), and the portal`s zoneless checkout, measured and recorded as witness.portalZonelessAttempt, counted the five pairs and the identity each end passed but took no receipt time, so it has a frame without a cost. A portal-backed verdict would therefore have to measure the same start-to-end difference this milestone measured on the counter fixture, and CHARTER.md`s portal clause does not reach the criterion until that target is re-pinned. The artefacts that carry it are extension/performance-narrator.js and the recorded brackets in research/raw/m040-work-events.json, whose frames.brackets and frames.rule state how a start is matched to its end. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/performance-narrator.test.mjs": its unmatched-start cases report the interval unmeasured rather than taking a duration from the next event, a reconstructed timestamp or a panel clock, and its zero-cost case reports a start and its matching end at the same recorded instant as zero rather than as missing.

claims.criterionText: The panel renders the frame's ordered work with the component identity and the measured cost in separate columns, and renders nothing it was not given: no cost for an unmeasured interval, no component for an unnamed one.
claims.reason: The surface this criterion names is the extension's DevTools panel, which is served from apps/angular-ai-devtools and is the surface that inspects a page - no insurance-portal route serves or renders it, so the portal is inspected by the panel and never the other way round, and CHARTER.md's portal clause does not reach the criterion. The artefact that carries it is apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-performance.ts, which renders the frame's ordered work as separate columns for the component identity and the measured cost and prints nothing a finding did not carry. The command that proves it is node --experimental-strip-types --test "scripts/panel-performance.test.mjs" with npx nx run angular-ai-devtools:test: the first holds each column to its own state and asserts that an unmeasured interval renders no number and an unnamed component renders no name, and the second holds the demo's sample fact to the recording, including that the same recorded frame rendered twice is byte-identical. The portal is not a page whose facts this criterion could be produced from: the zoneless checkout measured as witness.portalZonelessAttempt can now produce the frame the panel renders, and what no portal route provides is the panel itself, which is served from apps/angular-ai-devtools and inspects a page rather than being rendered by one.

claims.criterionText: `npm run check` and `npm test` pass at the head.
claims.reason: This criterion is the project gate itself, so it is answered by running the gate at the head of this milestone rather than by any page: no insurance-portal route whose facts are a test run exists, and CHARTER.md's portal clause therefore does not reach it - a portal-backed verdict would still be evidence about a page rather than about the gate. The artefacts that carry it are research/raw/m040-verdict-claims.json, this file, which is what lets scripts/overlay-verdict-claims.test.mjs check the milestone's claims instead of failing on a missing recording, and the suites the milestone landed. The command that proves it is npm run check && npm test, and the result is recorded in T005's Log rather than in a verdict.
